title: Make a decision
summary: Configure a rule that opens a gate only when every required condition is true.

scenario.briefing: The server room gate needs a rule. Access is allowed only when the badge is valid and it has not expired. Anything else must be rejected.

objectives.description: Choose a rule that matches every access case.
Explain how AND differs from OR.

hints: Test each candidate rule against all four badge cases.
The word and means both facts must hold.
An expired valid badge is still a reject. An invalid active badge is also a reject.
Choose the rule that requires valid and not expired. Only the first case is allowed.

misconceptions.description: Using OR when both conditions are required.
misconceptions.feedback: OR allows access when only one condition holds. That lets expired or invalid badges through. The policy needs both conditions.

misconceptions.description: Confusing AND with OR in natural language.
misconceptions.feedback: AND is true only when both sides are true. OR is true when at least one side is true.

sections.title: Conditions choose a path
sections.body: A condition tests evidence and selects an outcome. The gate checks two facts: whether the badge is valid and whether it has expired. The result depends on both.

sections.title: AND and OR are different
sections.body: AND requires every part to be true. OR requires at least one part to be true. Access rules are often security-sensitive, so a small logical mistake can admit the wrong person.

vocabulary.definition: A test that produces true or false.
True only when both operands are true.
True when at least one operand is true.

steps.title: Configure the gate
steps.prompt: Choose the rule that produces the required outcome for every badge case.

rules.label: Allow when the badge is valid
Allow when the badge has not expired
Allow when the badge is valid OR not expired
Allow when the badge is valid AND not expired

steps.explanation: Only the AND rule allows the valid, active badge and rejects the other three cases.

steps.title: AND or OR?
steps.prompt: Select every statement that is true.

statements.label: A AND B is true only when both A and B are true.
A OR B can be true when only A is true.
A AND B is true when either one is true.
NOT simply reverses true and false.

steps.explanation: AND requires both operands. OR needs at least one. NOT reverses the value.

steps.title: A different policy
steps.prompt: The delivery dock opens when a parcel is expected OR a courier is present, but never after quiet hours. Quiet hours are a separate rejection check. Which shape does this policy have?

options.label: (expected OR courier present) AND NOT quiet hours
expected AND courier present AND quiet hours

quiz.explanation: Either arrival condition can open the dock, and the quiet-hours rejection must also be false.

hints: Find the two alternatives that each allow entry.
Quiet hours must block both alternatives.
Combine the alternatives with OR, then require NOT quiet hours.
The policy is (expected OR courier) AND NOT quiet hours.

accessibility.summary: Rules are radio options with their full text. The expected outcomes table is a real table with headers.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Use arrow keys within the radio group, then Tab to the test button.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: Every rule announces its full wording. Results state which cases allow and which reject.
